solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Maybe the elder Bush pissed about end of war

indicators.note: about means around, so the reshuffled name wraps round the kept letter
pissed is slang for drunk, and a drunk word staggers into a new order

parts.note: the president's surname taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word means only its final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter of war

explanation.surface: George Bush senior, drunk, rambling about the end of a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The elder Bush' reads as George H. W. Bush, but the definition is 'Maybe the elder': an elder is a kind of bush. SHUB with R inside spells SHRUB.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a common flowering bush, so it is one example of a woody garden plant of this kind.

clue.text: Jetsam ovaries? Shows contribution of little boiler

indicators.note: the answer is shown as a contribution made by the words before, each lending some of its letters

parts.note: the run of letters starting near the end of Jetsam and continuing into ovaries

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about flotsam-like body parts, with a pseudo-scientific 'contribution' line.
explanation.walkthrough: Jet(SAM OVAR)ies spells SAMOVAR across the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: A samovar is a Russian tea urn that heats water, so it is a small domestic boiler.

clue.text: Shag's a jolly flier?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang verb for having sex with someone
second meaning: the pirate flag called the Jolly ..., which flies from a mast

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that a randy person is a cheerful fellow who gets about.
explanation.walkthrough: The Jolly Roger is the skull-and-crossbones pirate flag; 'flier' is a flag flying, not a pilot. The answer also means to have sex in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is British slang for sex and is also the name completing the pirate flag's title.

clue.text: Not a reputable place, making one of 25 swap political sides

indicators.note: changing political sides means right is exchanged for left, one letter traded for another

parts.note: 25-across is BRETHREN, and one of them is a single member
the right-hand R gives way to L for left

explanation.surface: A disreputable venue where a union comrade defects from one party to another.
explanation.walkthrough: BROTHER with its R (right) swapped for L (left) gives BROTHEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A brothel is a house of prostitution, hardly a respectable establishment.

clue.text: Drop behind someone in a hurry

parts.note: a teardrop, a drop from the eye
British slang for the backside

explanation.surface: Someone dropping back behind a person who is rushing along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop behind' reads as falling back; it is TEAR plus ARSE. A tearaway or tear-arse is British slang for someone who rushes about recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear-arse is British slang for a person who dashes about frantically, always rushing.

clue.text: Maybe outgoing banker's enhanced reward executed: "on a high — getting holiday place abroad!"

parts.note: to top someone is slang for killing them
up means elated
a pension is a continental boarding house or small hotel

explanation.surface: A retiring banker's bonus pension cheerfully described as a high-living holiday abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A pension in France or Italy is a modest guesthouse, so the last piece is the same word read in its continental sense. Bankers' boosted retirement payouts were a satirical target after the crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A pension that has been boosted is the extra retirement pay an outgoing banker might be given.

clue.text: Court prat embraces what's not supposed to matter

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first word wraps its arms round the second

parts.note: a prat is a fool, an ass
from the saying that size doesn't matter

explanation.surface: A fool in a courtroom gripping something supposedly unimportant, with a smutty undertone.
explanation.walkthrough: AS(SIZE)S: the cliché 'size doesn't matter' supplies the inner word. The Assizes were periodic county courts in England and Wales until 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: The Assizes were the travelling courts of England and Wales, held in each county by visiting judges.

clue.text: People at a meeting, possibly climax with ecstasy in disgusting state

indicators.note: in places the climax and drug inside the jumbled letters
something disgusting is in a foul mess, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
the end is a climax, possibly
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Delegates at a conference reaching a drug-fuelled climax and getting into a revolting state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' flags that a climax is only one kind of ending. E for ecstasy is standard slang for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendees are those present at an event, so they are the people at a meeting.

clue.text: Grade and Brenda hosting Name the Drug-taker

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the joined words take in the next letter

parts.note: to grade is to sort
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Two named people, Michael Grade and Brenda, presenting a show called Name the Drug-taker.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Grade was a TV executive, so the capitals suggest people; Brenda is Private Eye's long-running name for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorter is someone who sniffs a drug such as cocaine up the nose.

clue.text: Head of shit face follower of 'WH' in Private Eye

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the first letter of shit
mug is slang for face

explanation.surface: A crude description of a self-satisfied face in Private Eye's pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye calls the retailer WH Smith 'WH Smug', so the answer follows WH in the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Private Eye's running nickname for the newsagent chain is WH Smug, so this word comes after WH there.

clue.text: Work situation required for Labour after next general election?

definitions.text: required for Labour after next general election?

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a situation is a position

explanation.surface: A job vacancy notice for the Labour Party after the next general election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work situation required' reads like a job-seeker's small ad; the definition is a jibe that Labour will sit on the other side of the Commons after losing.
explanation.definitionFit: A party that loses a general election becomes the Opposition, the main non-governing group in Parliament.

clue.text: Oxford protector possibly needs lots of balls and a garden implement

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls
a hoe is a weeding tool
joins the two pieces

explanation.surface: Something guarding Oxford University requires plenty of nerve and a gardening tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' suggests the university, but an oxford is a lace-up shoe. In cricket an over is six deliveries, so 'lots of balls' is several overs.
explanation.definitionFit: An overshoe is a cover worn over footwear such as an oxford brogue to protect it from wet.

clue.text: Some pint-size nit has climax

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are used, a run taken from inside them

parts.note: the run from the end of pint-size, through nit, into has

explanation.surface: A tiny louse egg reaches its peak, a mock-heroic moment.
explanation.walkthrough: pint-si(ZE NIT H)as: 'has' supplies only its first letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: The zenith is the highest point of something, the peak or culmination.

clue.text: Underwear (reversed) Ms Hurley put on bollocks, which get crushed

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment

indicators.note: the bracketed word tells you the name after it is read backwards

parts.note: the actress Liz Hurley
both are slang for testicles

explanation.surface: Liz Hurley's underwear, inside out, worn on a man's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: BRA, then LIZ reversed to ZIL, then NUTS. 'Which get crushed' is cheeky: both these hard-shelled nuts and testicles can be crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil nuts have very hard shells and must be cracked or crushed with a nutcracker to be eaten.

clue.text: Get i.e. 'rocks' covered with popped zits — that's the spirit!

indicators.note: being covered with something means it surrounds you on the outside
rocks as a verb means shakes about, so the letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: popped spots burst apart, so their letters are scattered too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grotty instruction to cover something in burst spots, ending with a cheery exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: Both lots of letters are shuffled: one set sits inside the other, splitting the spots after their first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeitgeist is German for the spirit of the times, the defining mood of an era.

clue.text: Subprime finally ballsed up our money

indicators.note: finally keeps just the closing letter of the word before

parts.note: the last letter of subprime

indicators.note: ballsed up is slang for botched, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Subprime mortgages finally wrecked our currency, a banking-crisis complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the 2008 crash caused by subprime lending.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the single currency of much of the European Union, a form of cash.

clue.text: Fruity thing's unattractive broadcast

indicators.note: what is broadcast is heard rather than read, so we go by sound

parts.note: unattractive means plain-looking; the fruit's name is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A camp person's appearance is described as unattractive on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a tangelo with wrinkled rind; its trade name was coined from its looks.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a citrus fruit, a hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine, so it is a fruity thing.

clue.text: Party deserting Gordon "are awful," he whimpers

indicators.note: awful means dreadful, so the letters are badly disordered
to desert is to leave, so those letters walk out of the name

parts.note: a do is a party; these letters leave
Gordon Brown's first name taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown, deserted by party colleagues, whines that they are awful.
explanation.walkthrough: GORDON loses DO to leave GRON, then GRON with ARE is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A groaner is one who moans or complains, so one who whimpers.

clue.text: Strict control about to be imposed on Fleet Street gets no one's backing

parts.note: re means concerning, about
Fleet Street is the traditional home of London's newspapers

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so those words are read from the end

parts.note: no plus I for one

explanation.surface: A complaint about state control of the newspapers that no one supports.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + PRESS + NO I written backwards (ION). Fleet Street is the London street where national papers were based, so it stands for the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Repression is forcible subjugation or restraint, harsh control of people or ideas.

clue.text: Also-ran Cherie hugs man with beastly spread?

indicators.note: to hug is to hold within, so the answer sits held inside the words

parts.note: the end of also-ran running into Cherie

explanation.surface: Cherie Blair, a losing candidate, embracing a man with an unpleasantly large belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly spread' suggests a gut; it is a ranch with livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rancher owns a large spread of land stocked with cattle, so beasts roam his spread.

clue.text: Good time to penetrate butt, being tied up

indicators.note: to penetrate is to go into, so the first pair goes inside

parts.note: the butt is the end of something, as a cigarette butt
G is the abbreviation for good
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A smutty bondage scenario: a good time for anal sex while bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' looks like a bottom in the surface, but it is the end of something, like a cigarette butt.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engaged is busy and occupied, which is what being tied up means figuratively.

clue.text: Obama's openings against debts hardly a surprise

indicators.note: openings are starts, so only the leading letters of the name are kept

parts.note: the first two letters of Obama
V for versus
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: Obama's early moves against national debts were predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: Unusually, 'openings' supplies two letters from one word rather than the first letter of several.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious is plain and expected, hardly a surprise to anyone.

clue.text: Endlessly stuff working woman who's repulsive

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to gorge is to stuff oneself
on as in switched on, functioning

explanation.surface: A sexist jibe about an off-putting woman who never stops eating while at work.
explanation.walkthrough: GORGE loses its last letter and ON is added. In Greek myth the Gorgons, such as Medusa, were hideous women.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorgon is figuratively a fearsome or ugly woman, after the monsters of Greek myth.

clue.text: Defeatist, pissed, go native, getting drug for nothing

indicators.note: pissed is slang for drunk, so the words reel into new order
getting one thing for another means a trade, one letter exchanged

parts.note: taken as written
E for ecstasy, which replaces the O
O is a zero, nothing; it is swapped out

explanation.surface: A drunk, gloomy expat who has gone native and takes drugs for free.
explanation.walkthrough: In GO NATIVE the O becomes E, and the result GENATIVE is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: A negative attitude is pessimistic, expecting failure, which is what a defeatist has.

clue.text: 10% boob man

parts.note: both are slang for a breast
he is a male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man who is one tenth breast, a crude absurdity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boob' could mean a blunder, but here it is a breast.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce or income paid to the church, hence ten per cent.

clue.text: A favourite party political activity, if gin drunk with thing out

indicators.note: drunk words lurch about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: out as in out of order, so these letters are also rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Party politics described as a favourite pastime of drinking gin and kicking someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a drinks do, which the gin supports; it is a political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Infighting is conflict between members of the same group, rife within political parties.

clue.text: Spike, getting end away: "God!"

indicators.note: the end goes away, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a thorn is a sharp spike on a plant

explanation.surface: Spike Milligan, or a man named Spike, having sex and crying out 'God!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex; here it simply drops the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder, wielder of the hammer Mjolnir.

clue.text: Brown: "Have to go with three pisspoor northern union colleagues"

parts.note: BR is the abbreviation for brown

indicators.note: something pisspoor is shoddy work, so the letters come out badly arranged

parts.note: taken as written
N for northern

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown saying he must side with three useless northern trade unionists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like Gordon Brown but gives only its abbreviation. Trade unionists traditionally address one another as brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Brethren is the old plural of brother, the term of address between fellow trade union members.

clue.text: Gordon's guts turned over — 'e's acquired start of spending habit

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so those letters run the other way
guts are innards, so only the central letters of the name are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of Gordon
cockney he's, written without its h

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter only

parts.note: the first letter of spending

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's stomach churning because he has picked up a spending habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guts' takes the two central letters of a six-letter name. 'Habit' reads as a vice, but it is a garment, as a nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a long robe worn by monks or nuns, a type of garment.
